title: Boiling and condensation: the boiling curve and the critical heat flux
examples: What is the critical heat flux?
Why do water drops dance on a very hot pan?

curves.label: Water at 1 atm
curves.ask: What does the boiling curve show for water?

explain.say: Watch a pan of water heat up. First nothing, then tiny bubbles on the bottom, then a rolling boil. In 1934 Shiro Nukiyama in Japan measured how much heat a hot wire can pass to boiling water, and found a strange curve. Look at the particles: bubbles forming on a hot surface.

draw.text: Boiling and condensation: the boiling curve and the critical heat flux

explain.say: The graph is the boiling curve. Along the bottom is the excess temperature, how much hotter the surface is than 100 degrees. At a few degrees, heat leaves by plain convection. Then bubbles form at tiny pits in the surface: nucleate boiling. Each bubble carries away latent heat and stirs the water, so the heat flux soars. See the steep climb?

curves.label: Water at 1 atm
curves.ask: What does the boiling curve show for water?

draw.text: Nucleate boiling: h can reach tens of thousands of W/m²·K

explain.say: At about 30 degrees excess, the heat flux peaks near 1.26 megawatts per square metre: the critical heat flux. Push harder and bubbles merge into a vapour blanket that insulates the surface. The flux falls! Far right, a stable vapour film forms: film boiling. Why might a boiler tube melt if you pass the peak?

curves.label: Water at 1 atm
curves.ask: What does the boiling curve show for water?

draw.text: Critical heat flux for water at 1 atm ≈ 1.26 MW/m²

explain.say: Because the vapour film blocks the heat, the tube temperature jumps by hundreds of degrees. Nuclear and power-plant engineers stay well below that peak. The reverse process is condensation: steam gives up its latent heat on a cool surface. See the particles gathering into liquid?

draw.text: Kettle: 2000 W / 2257 kJ/kg ≈ 0.89 g/s of steam

explain.say: Great job. Dropwise condensation, with beads on the surface, can transfer heat several times faster than a full film. Fun link: water drops skating on a very hot pan show the Leidenfrost effect, floating on their own vapour film. Exam tip: latent heat of water at 1 atm is 2257 kilojoules per kilogram.

draw.text: A 2 kW kettle boils off about 53 g of water per minute

faq.a: A graph of heat flux against excess surface temperature for a boiling liquid. It shows natural convection, nucleate boiling up to a peak, transition boiling and film boiling.

faq.q: What does the boiling curve show for water?
faq.a: For water at one atmosphere, heat flux climbs steeply in nucleate boiling to a peak of about 1.26 megawatts per square metre near 30 degrees excess, falls in transition boiling, then slowly rises again in film boiling.

faq.q: What is the critical heat flux?
faq.a: The highest heat flux nucleate boiling can carry before vapour blankets the surface. For water at one atmosphere it is about 1.26 megawatts per square metre.

faq.q: Why do water drops dance on a very hot pan?
faq.a: Above the Leidenfrost point the drop sits on a thin layer of its own vapour, which insulates it and lets it skate around without touching the metal.
Condensation where vapour forms separate beads instead of a continuous liquid film. The bare metal between drops lets heat pass several times faster.

facts: Shiro Nukiyama published the first boiling curve in 1934.
The latent heat of vaporisation of water at 1 atm is about 2257 kJ/kg.

quiz.say: A 3 kilowatt kettle is boiling. About how much water does it turn to steam each minute? The latent heat is 2257 kilojoules per kilogram.
quiz.show: 3 kW kettle, h_fg = 2257 kJ/kg. Steam made per minute?
quiz.why: 3 kJ/s ÷ 2257 kJ/kg = 1.33 g/s; × 60 ≈ 80 g per minute.

wrong.1: That is the amount per second, not per minute.
wrong.2: A factor of ten slipped in the arithmetic.

quiz.say: What happens if a heated surface goes past the critical heat flux?
quiz.show: A heated surface goes past the critical heat flux. What happens?

options.show: A vapour film forms and the surface temperature jumps
options.say: A vapour film forms and the surface temperature jumps

options.show: Boiling stops and the water freezes
options.say: Boiling stops and the water freezes

options.show: The heat transfer coefficient rises sharply
options.say: The heat transfer coefficient rises sharply

quiz.why: Vapour blankets the surface and insulates it, so the surface must get much hotter to pass the same heat.

wrong.1: The water stays at boiling temperature; it does not freeze.
wrong.2: h falls past the critical heat flux, it does not rise.
